ledger.note: 1899 (19 January): Britain and Egypt agree to administer the Sudan jointly. 'On 19 January 1899, an agreement between the UK and Egypt relating to the administration of the Sudan defined "Soudan" as the "territories south of the 22nd parallel of latitude"'; the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan page gives the condominium as 'Established: 19 June 1899' and Kitchener's campaigns 'from 1896 to 1898'. The Mahdist state fell at Omdurman on 2 September 1898 (Mahdist War page: the Anglo-Egyptians 'reached Omdurman, the Mahdist capital, on 2 September').

region.text: Suakin on the Red Sea coast

ledger.note: 1899 (10 July): Suakin goes to Sudan. A 10 July 1899 amendment 'gave Suakin to Sudan instead' of Egypt.

region.text: the Bishareen grazing land north of the 22nd parallel that Sudan administered from 1902, about 18,000 km2 including Halaib and Abu Ramad

ledger.note: 1902 (4 November): Sudan administers the Halaib land. 'On 4 November 1902, the UK drew a separate administrative boundary' that 'gave to Sudan the grazing land of another Beja subtribe, The Bishareen north of the line to administer', about 18,000 km2 including Halaib and Abu Ramad; Egypt kept regarding the 22nd parallel as the border.

region.text: the Lado Enclave, 'about 15,000 square miles (39,000 km2)'

ledger.note: 1910 (10 June): the Lado Enclave comes under the Sudan. 'On 10 June 1910, following Leopold's death, the district officially became a province of the' Anglo-Egyptian Sudan; it had been leased on 12 May 1894 to Leopold II, the lease running for Leopold's lifetime. The counterpart is the Belgian Congo: the enclave was 'administered by the Congo Free State and later by the Belgian Congo' (infobox 'Belgian Congo (1908–1910)'); the belgian-congo dossier records the 1910 loss (counterpart set by the reviewer, af-08-x review).

region.text: the southern half of the Lado Enclave, later the West Nile district of Uganda

ledger.note: 1912: the southern half of the Lado Enclave goes to Uganda. 'In 1912 the southern half of the Lado Enclave was ceded to Uganda, then a British protectorate.'

region.text: part of the enclave exchanged with Uganda for a stretch of the Upper Nile

ledger.note: 1914 (1 January): the Sudan-Uganda boundary is settled by an exchange. 'This was achieved on 1 January 1914 when Sudan formally exchanged part of the enclave for a stretch of the Upper Nile'; 'The area of the Lado Enclave integrated into Uganda was renamed West Nile'. The page does not say which stretch Sudan received or its size, so the outline change is not drawn.

'The present borders were established by an agreement signed in Rome on July 20, 1934' which 'transferred the administration of the Sarra triangle from Anglo-Egyptian Sudan to Italian Libya', 'approximately 30,000 square kilometers'.

1956 (1 January): the condominium becomes the independent Sudan. Infobox 'Independence: 1 January 1956'; 'In October 1954, Egypt and the UK signed a treaty granting Sudan independence on 1 January 1956'. Self-government came on '22 October 1952' (infobox) or 'in March 1953' (body text), and an agreement among Egypt, the UK and Sudanese representatives was reached on 12 February 1953. The Republic of Sudan row starts on the same day.

wars.note: The war ran 1881-1899; only its last months fall in this state's life. Omdurman fell on 2 September 1898 (Mahdist State dossier).

wars.outcome: British victory: Sultan Ali Dinar killed in 1916 and Darfur incorporated (1916 on the main page, 1917 on the Darfur page).

certainty.note: The 22nd-parallel line of 1899 is a treaty line but the 1902 administrative line differs from it (Halaib); the southern and western frontiers of the Sudan with the Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and Chad are not on any page opened. The 1934 Rome agreement fixed the Libyan frontier sharply.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Anglo-Egyptian Sudan row (it lies inside the aggregate 'British Africa' 1885-1960), so every keyframe is new and built from modern outlines. Dates: the Halaib Triangle page gives the Condominium agreement as 19 January 1899, the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan infobox 19 June 1899; the dossier follows the page that quotes the agreement. The dossier ends on 1 January 1956, the day the Republic of Sudan row starts.
Not settled for want of a page: the southern frontier and how much of Equatoria and Bahr el Ghazal the Condominium actually held in 1899 (the keyframes draw the modern South Sudan outline from 1899, which is generous for the first years); the Sudan-Uganda exchange of 1914 (area unknown); the Egypt-Sudan boundary change at Wadi Halfa; the Ilemi triangle and Kafia Kingi; the 1924 events (the page only says Britain edged Egypt out 'almost completely by 1924' and divided the country into two 'from 1924 onwards'); Bahr el Ghazal's 1948 split from Equatoria is internal. Egypt as co-ruler is not drawn as a separate layer.
Counterparts needing dossiers: italian-libya (1911-1943) and uganda-protectorate (1894-1962, af-05 lists it). Gazetteer: 'Halaib Triangle', 'Lado Enclave', 'Sarra Triangle' (regions) and 'Suakin' (place) are real names the gazetteer lacks; the Darfur outline is the five Darfur admin-1 states.

Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026), Sarra Triangle. The name 'Sarra Triangle' is not in the gazetteer, so keyframe anglo-egyptian-sudan_1916 did not resolve (Darfur stayed british-africa 1917-1933) and the 1934 loss never took the land. Both specs now use a disc of 107 km (119 cells, 30,095 km2) around Ma'tan as-Sarra (21.68333 N, 21.83111 E; Ma'tan as-Sarra page: 'an oasis in the Kufra District municipality in the southeast corner of Libya', 'In 1934, Ma'tan as-Sarra was turned over as part of the Sarra Triangle to Fascist Italy'); the Sarra Triangle page gives the area ('approximately 30,000 square kilometers'), the agreement ('signed in Rome on July 20, 1934') and the district (Kufra) but no coordinates or vertices, and says Britain 'never held any de facto authority over the strip'. The disc is a stand-in of the right area, not the triangle's outline. ROUTE: italian-libya (keyframe italian-libya_1932 and its 1934 events) and italian-africa use the same unresolved name and need the same spec.
